stories.title: Indonesia keeps several airports closed but Anak Krakatau volcanic eruption is easing
stories.summary: Indonesia has more than 120 active volcanoes and frequently experiences eruptions due to its location along the Pacific “Ring of Fire.”
stories.article_text_excerpt: Indonesia kept several airports closed and shifted schools to remote learning on Monday though a volcanic eruption that halted 2,300 flights and coated areas with ash was subsiding.The continuous, 25-hour eruption of Anak Krakatau that produced a fountain of lava and a boom heard 700 kilometres away ended on Sunday, the country's Geological Agency said.But it remained active on Monday with moderate, intermittent eruptions, dark ash emissions and small, localised earthquakes, the agency said in a statement.Weather was obscuring visual observations of the eruption.AirNav Indonesia said tests showed volcanic ash present in the airspace around Jakarta and several other cities, prompting authorities to close eight airports until 6 pm on Monday, including the four commercial airports managed by state-owned operator InJourney Airports: Jakarta's international airports of Soekarno-Hatta and Halim Perdanakusuma, Husein Sastranegara in West Java and Radin Inten in Lampung on the southern tip of Sumatra.The closure disrupted about 2,300 flights and affected 268,539 passengers at the four airports managed by InJourney Airports, the company said.The eruption’s impact extended beyond air travel.

stories.title: In Saxony-Anhalt election, small parties will be kingmakers

On Sunday, the 1.7 million eligible voters in the eastern German state will decide whether the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party can form a state government for the first time. There hasn't been a head of government who belonged to a proven far-right party in post- World War II Germany — at neither federal nor state level. That would change if AfD lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund were to be elected to this position, since the Office for the Protection of the Constitution in Saxony-Anhalt already classified the AfD as such in 2023. Siegmund's chances of a historical triumph are high: For months, the AfD has been comfortably leading the polls with well over 40% of the vote.
